title: Formally Verifying Arithmetic Chisel Designs for All Bit Widths at Once
problem: Formal verification of arithmetic units in hardware designs faces state explosion problems due to bit widths, requiring expensive separate verification for each bit width. Low-level verification of Chisel arithmetic units remains inefficient and costly.
motivation: Chisel is increasingly used for high-level design of production RISC-V CPUs like RocketChip and XiangShan, but verification remains low-level and requires separate bit-width checks.
method: The approach transforms arithmetic Chisel designs into Scala software programs that preserve high-level features and simulate their behavior, then applies Stainless (a deductive formal verification tool for Scala) to verify correctness. This enables single verification passes covering all bit widths simultaneously rather than requiring separate verification for each width.
key_novelty: High-level formal verification of parameterized Chisel arithmetic designs for all bit widths at once through transformation to Scala and deductive verification, avoiding state explosion.
contributions: Transformation methodology to convert Chisel arithmetic designs to Scala programs suitable for deductive formal verification
Formal verification of dividers and multipliers in RocketChip and XiangShan RISC-V processors
Parameterized verification approach handling all bit widths simultaneously in a single proof
Significantly lower verification cost compared to proof-assistant-based approaches like Kami

metrics.other: verification cost reduction versus Kami-based approaches

limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: High-level formal verification of parameterized hardware arithmetic
